_comment: Maps appsec-protocols security controls to OWASP ASVS 5.0.0 requirement IDs. tier: 1=PR gate (static), 2=post-deploy probe, 3=test-suite contract, 4=attested manual. Every asvs id is validated against the released standard by build-coverage.py.

controls.title: Hide API keys
controls.note: ASVS treats this as secrets management generally; the control is narrower and sharper - no secret in a client bundle, and NEXT_PUBLIC_/VITE_/EXPO_PUBLIC_ vars are public identifiers only.

controls.title: Purge Git secrets
controls.note: PARTIAL. V13.4.1 covers not deploying .git metadata; V13.3.4 covers rotation. ASVS 5.0 has no requirement to scan or scrub version-control history for committed secrets. The rotate-then-scrub ordering is not in the standard.

controls.title: Use the public/anon key client-side
controls.note: Least-privilege secret access, specialised to the BaaS anon-vs-service-role split that ASVS does not name.

controls.title: Enable row-level security
controls.note: ASVS states the outcome (data-specific access restricted at a trusted service layer); the control names the mechanism (RLS enabled AND a policy present) and the ORM-only fallback.

controls.title: Encrypt sensitive data
controls.note: ASVS V11 is substantially deeper here - key lifecycle, crypto agility, authenticated encryption modes. The control covers column-level at-rest encryption only.

controls.title: Enforce server-side auth
controls.note: Direct match.

controls.title: Lock record access (IDOR)
controls.note: Direct match. V8.2.2 names IDOR explicitly.

controls.title: Block field tampering (mass assignment)
controls.note: Direct match. V8.2.3 covers the authorization side (broken object property level authorization), V15.3.3 the coding side.

controls.title: Secure session cookies
controls.note: ASVS additionally requires the __Host- prefix (V3.3.3), which this control does not mention. Worth adopting.

controls.title: Hash (and salt) passwords
controls.note: Direct match. The control adds the scrypt/pbkdf2 no-embedded-salt footgun and the pepper option, neither of which ASVS calls out.

controls.title: Rate limit login
controls.note: The control's opinionated call - progressive backoff over hard lockout, because lockout is itself a DoS - is a position ASVS does not take.

controls.title: Add bot protection
controls.note: PARTIAL. ASVS requires anti-automation to be documented and implemented but does not prescribe CAPTCHA or server-side token verification.

controls.title: Verify JWTs properly
controls.note: Strong match - ASVS V9 is a dedicated self-contained-token chapter. The control covers 6 of its 7 requirements.

controls.title: Configure OAuth correctly
controls.note: MOST UNDER-COVERED. ASVS V10 has 36 requirements; this control meaningfully addresses 8. Anything doing serious OAuth work should read V10 directly.

controls.title: Parameterize queries
controls.note: V1.2.4 covers SQL, HQL, NoSQL and Cypher in one requirement. The control's NoSQL operator-injection treatment (type confusion, not string escaping) is more concrete.

controls.title: Validate all input
controls.note: The control's validate-on-input/escape-on-output stance matches V1.1.2 (encoding as a final step before the interpreter).

controls.title: Escape user content
controls.note: Direct match.

controls.title: Restrict file uploads
controls.note: ASVS V5 adds archive handling (zip bombs, symlinks, uncompressed-size caps) and pixel-flood limits that this control omits.

controls.title: Trim API responses
controls.note: Direct match.

controls.title: Add security headers
controls.note: PARTIAL GAP IN ASVS: the control requires a restrictive Permissions-Policy; ASVS 5.0 has no requirement for that header.

controls.title: Force HTTPS
controls.note: ASVS is MORE precise here: V4.1.2 says only user-facing endpoints should auto-redirect HTTP to HTTPS, since redirecting API endpoints teaches clients that plaintext is acceptable. The control says redirect all. ASVS is right.

controls.title: Scan dependencies
controls.note: ASVS frames this as documented remediation time frames plus an SBOM; the control frames it as a failing CI gate. Complementary.

controls.title: Vet the package itself, not just its CVEs
controls.note: MOST DIFFERENTIATED. V15.2.4 requires components come from the expected repository, which is adjacent. ASVS 5.0 does not address typosquatting, install-script payloads, or AI-hallucinated package names (slopsquatting) as a distinct class.

controls.title: Add CSRF protection
controls.note: The control's decision rule - cookie auth triggers CSRF defence, pure Bearer does not - is clearer than ASVS's framing.

controls.title: Limit request size
controls.note: PARTIAL. ASVS covers file sizes and resource-demanding functionality; a generic HTTP body cap is implied rather than required.

controls.title: Rate limit the whole API, not just login
controls.note: V2.4.1 is the anchor (anti-automation against excessive calls). The control adds the keying guidance - per-IP collapses against a botnet, per-user is the real budget.

controls.title: Close the unintended surface
controls.note: BEST-COVERED CONTROL. ASVS V13.4 enumerates this more thoroughly than the control does.

controls.title: Lock down non-production environments
controls.note: GAP IN ASVS. ASVS scopes itself to the application under verification and has no requirement that preview/staging deploys carry auth, a noindex header, separate credentials, or non-production data. This control has no real ASVS counterpart.

controls.title: Treat model output as untrusted input
controls.note: NO ASVS COVERAGE. ASVS 5.0 has no LLM or prompt-injection chapter. The listed IDs are the generic principles the control specialises (authorization at a trusted layer, no eval, no shell interpolation) - not requirements about AI. OWASP addresses this in a separate project, the LLM Top 10.

controls.title: Cap AI usage and cost
controls.note: NO ASVS COVERAGE. Financial denial-of-wallet on metered model endpoints is not an ASVS concern; the anti-automation requirements are the closest generic analogue.

controls.title: Block path traversal
controls.note: Direct match. V1.1.1 (decode once, before validation) is the requirement that explains why naive '..' filtering fails.

controls.title: Prevent SSRF
controls.note: Direct match. The control adds resolve-then-connect (DNS rebinding) and the cloud metadata endpoint specifically.

controls.title: Never build shell commands from user input
controls.note: Direct match.

controls.title: Don't deserialise untrusted data into objects
controls.note: Direct match.

controls.title: Keep an audit trail
controls.note: Direct match. ASVS V16 is more thorough on log format, time synchronisation and log inventory.

controls.title: Keep secrets out of logs - and logs out of public reach
controls.note: Direct match.

controls.title: Back up, and prove the restore
controls.note: NO ASVS COVERAGE. ASVS 5.0 contains no backup or restore requirement - it verifies the application, not the operational practice around it. V14.2.7 covers retention and deletion, which is the opposite concern. This control has no counterpart in the standard.

controls.title: Monitor and alert
controls.note: PARTIAL. V16.4.3 requires logs be shipped to a separate system for detection and alerting. Nothing in ASVS requires proving an alert actually reaches a human, which is this control's entire verification step.

controls.title: Run everything least-privilege
controls.note: PARTIAL. ASVS covers least privilege for secret access and non-default service credentials. Database grants, cloud IAM scoping, firewall default-deny and SSH key-only are infrastructure, which ASVS deliberately excludes.

controls.title: Isolate tenants
controls.note: Direct match, and ASVS states it in one requirement. The control adds the operational surfaces that leak quietly - cache keys, search indexes, background jobs, file paths.

controls.title: Verify webhooks
controls.note: PARTIAL GAP. V4.1.5 covers per-message digital signatures at L3 only; V11.2.4 covers constant-time comparison. ASVS has no requirement for webhook replay windows, event-id idempotency, or verifying over the raw pre-parse body.

controls.title: Keep payment authority on the server
controls.note: PARTIAL. ASVS handles this as generic business-logic validation at a trusted service layer. It has no payment-specific requirement, so price tampering, coupon re-validation at charge time and webhook-as-source-of-truth are specialisations, not restatements.
